title: Port language-aware tokenization and exact citation lookup
note: Native proposal validation, accepted merge and task completion remain separate required gates. This receipt does not mark the backlog complete.
known_limitations: This receipt is not a native completion or merge receipt.
tokenize.ts, citation.ts, and tokenizer-parity.test.ts are uncommitted working-tree files. site_revision is HEAD before those edits.
artifacts/ is gitignored, so this receipt is on disk and is not part of git status.

Default tokenize() with no options matches country_laws_ir/tokenize.py at commit 2ea4ca6804b3c4cc44e43d0539f4c3fcae011747: NFKD, drop Unicode 15.0.0 combining class non-zero, lowercase, then ASCII [0-9A-Za-z] runs.

That pinned strategy deletes letters that do not fold into ASCII. ø, æ, ł, ð, þ, đ, and ß split or disappear. Cyrillic, Greek, Hebrew, Arabic, Indic, Han, Hangul, kana, and Thai letters are dropped except for ASCII digits left behind.

Pinned folding also decomposes Hangul syllables into jamo and strips kana dakuten and Thai tone marks before the ASCII filter deletes the letters. The hangul, kana, and southeast-asian-run strategies do not do that.
Selecting a language, or any strategy other than fts5-unicode61, keeps native letters and diacritics. It is not the pinned index tokenizer. An explicit fts5-unicode61 strategy wins over a language.
No stemming, lemmatization, stopword removal, synonym expansion, transliteration, cross-language recall, Turkish locale casing, or ß to ss expansion.

No dictionary segmentation for Chinese, Japanese, Thai, Lao, Khmer, or Myanmar, and no Japanese morphological analysis. cjk-unigram emits one token per Han character. Southeast Asian strategies keep a maximal run. identifier keeps a Han run whole.
No Arabic, Hebrew, or Persian orthographic folding. Harakat, niqqud, and tatweel are kept by those strategies. Tatweel is not removed.
Indic strategies do not split on virama. ICU word boundaries are not used.

The combining-class table is Unicode 15.0.0 from the pinned CPython unicodedata. Host NFKD is Node's Unicode normalization. A mark with combining class 0, such as U+034F, is kept by the pinned fold. The tested compatibility decompositions (ligatures, circled digits, numero sign, micro sign, fullwidth letters) matched the pin on this Node.
query.py MAX_QUERY_TERMS is a retrieval cap. tokenize() does not apply it.
normalizeCiteKey matches citations.py. It deletes non-ASCII instead of folding diacritics, so Código becomes c digo, not codigo. officialCitation and nativeIdentifier keep the original identifier.
ORS 1.010 and Or. Rev. Stat. § 1.010 do not share a citeKey.
Bluebook text is emitted only for pinned rows with emit bluebook. In bluebook_t2.json that is usa and united states. Unknown jurisdictions are not given an invented Bluebook form.
The United States Bluebook form does not include the title number. Title is only required. The official citation carries the identifier.
Pinpoint suppression is a case-insensitive substring test, so art. 1 is treated as already present inside art. 12.
Slug is consulted before country and jurisdiction.
Non-Latin official text can collapse to an ASCII pinpoint citeKey such as art 1. Format any therefore matches that key. Format native does not consult citeKey.
A pinpoint with no eli, official identifier, identifier, or title has status unknown and is not returned by lookup.

Format native, plus optional exact sourceRevision and jurisdiction filters, are additions. duckdb cite_search has no jurisdiction or revision predicate and no native format. Formats any, bluebook, and official still match citeKey, as cite_search does.
Year is the caller year, or the first four digits of snapshotDate when year is empty, matching the normalize.py call site rather than citations.py alone.
Lookup is exact and in memory. It does not read parquet, DuckDB, or a BM25 index.
